chunks: And by this chain from Muhammad ibn Ahmad who said: It was narrated to me by Abu Ya'qub Yusuf ibn al-Sukht from al-Hasan ibn Sahl al-Basri from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) and saw in his hand a ring with a turquoise stone, its inscription being 'For Allah is the dominion'. I kept gazing at it, so he said: 'What is it that you are looking at? This is a stone that Gabriel gifted to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from Paradise, and the Messenger of Allah gifted it to Ali (peace be upon him). Do you know its name?' I said: 'Turquoise.' He said: 'This is its name in Persian. Do you know its name in Arabic?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It is Al-Zafar (Victory).'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the word Firuzaj in Arabic according to Imam Musa al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to highlight the spiritual merit of wearing a turquoise ring, linking the stone's celestial origin—gifted by Gabriel to the Prophet and then to Ali—to the concept of divine victory. The linguistic connection between 'Firuzaj' and 'Al-Zafar' serves as a symbolic reminder of the Imamate's role in securing spiritual triumph for the faithful.
